what_is_said: Palace loan history (Council case and order, 1903-05). In 1891 the late Maharaja lent the matha Rs 1,25,000 at 4% repayable at Rs 12,500 a year. By 1896 it was reduced to Rs 80,027-2-0 and then raised again to the original sum by the Maharani-Regent; the matha spent this on jewels, not creditors. Instalments were waived until May 1904, when the debt stood at Rs 1,31,812-13-0. The Agent's requests (instalment cut from Rs 12,500 to Rs 5,000 without interest, or the State tasdik raised from Rs 6,000 to Rs 12,000) were refused. Order (10 Oct 1905): on punctual payment of Rs 12,500 a year, that year's interest is remitted.

what_is_said: June-July 1907 tour in Mysore District: whether the Swami might be taken into Srirangapatna fort at a sahukar's invitation. what_is_said: Proposed visit to the Belur (Chennakesava) temple, 1924. Sri Vaishnavas and temple servants had disputed the Swami's right to enter the garbhagriha and do puja in 1891, and the late Swami had avoided the temple. As the situation was 'delicate', Government advised the Swami not to visit the temple without the consent of the communities concerned. The DC Kadur reported that he had decided not to visit it. The 1895 Srirangapatna papers are reprinted for reference.
quote: Kadur District, stating that His Holiness has decided not to visit the Belur temple.
notes: Sri Vaishnava-Smārta temple-rights dispute.

Government held that the cess should go to the Government treasury for the District Board, and the amount was paid into the Koppa treasury.

Srikantha Sastry asked the Chief Secretary (3 Nov 1927) for military escort and police arrangements for the Jagadguru's visits from the Sankar Mutt, Bangalore, to receive bhiksha and padapuja at the Basavangudi bungalows of G. Srinivasa Iyer (Chief Court judge, 4 Nov) and N. Krishna Rao (Member of Council, 6 Nov), citing precedents of 1907 and 1911. The 1907 order (Muzrai Secretary, 16 May 1907) gave an escort of the strength used in 1895: 4 NCOs and 30 rank and file plus 6 NCOs and 24 rank and file with a full band 29 strong.

what_is_said: On the Jagadguru's arrival at Shimoga (10 Jan 1928) the Reception Committee claimed that he was entitled to an infantry Guard of Honour; the Deputy Commissioner, Shimoga, sought orders and the Mutt wired for a guard 'as on previous occasion'. Government allowed a guard if there was precedent; the DC traced G.O. No. 1760-64 of 13 Jan 1911 (guard of honour and military escort at Bangalore, and also at Shimoga in 1911) and the 2nd Battalion furnished a Guard of Honour and military escort for the procession in Shimoga town.
quote: Jagadguru of Sringeri Mutt, Mr. Raghavia, a leading - Advocate of Shimoga and Secretary of the Reception Com- mittee wrote to me on the %th stating that His Holiness is entitled to a Guard of Honour by the Infantry

what_is_said: The Muzrai Commissioner (2 Nov 1927) recommended that Rs 500 (not the Rs 800 asked) be sanctioned from Muzrai funds, debited to the Sivaganga Mutt's funds, for the bhiksha and padapuja of the Sringeri Jagadguru during a two-day halt at Sivaganga on his return to Sringeri; the Sivaganga Mutt could not pay interest on loans already given.

notes: Concerns the Sivaganga Mutt (a separate Smarta mutt under Muzrai education committee) hosting the Sringeri Swami; catalogue calls it a lease, but it is a loan/sanction. Approved by G.O. No. 720-21/Muz. 110-27-2 of Nov 1927 (cited in next file).

Of the Rs 500, Rs 300 was offered as padapuja and a silver tray with about Rs 100 presented; the Jagadguru examined the young Sivaganga Swami and suggested he study Vedanta at Sringeri under the Jagadguru.

what_is_said: The Agent asked Government to reconsider the order of 28 Apr 1928 making Sringeri a minor municipality with its entire tax income devoted to municipal purposes, which took away the moiety of municipal collections that the Mutt had enjoyed under order No. 13801-4 of 13 Feb 1893 until 1917. He asked that the Mutt be relieved of its agreement to meet the cost of the Local Fund Dispensary at Sringeri; the file discusses the Mutt paying three-fourths of the dispensary cost and a revised share.

notes: The Jahgirdar (the Swami) refused in 1917 to give up the moiety. The final contribution ratio for the dispensary is not clear in the OCR.

what_is_said: Dispute over the Barr infantry guard attached for about 40 years to guard the Saradamba temple and the jewels given by the Mysore kings. The Mutt had paid Rs 56 a month, but G.O. of 2 Apr 1924 (confirmed 14 Jul/Aug 1924) required the full cost of Rs 120 a month from 1 Apr 1924, leaving arrears of Rs 3,190-5-0. The Agent asked for the guard free, citing a free Palace guard at the Parakala Mutt, Mysore. Government (Financial Secretary, 13 Dec 1928) refused to reopen the matter. It held that the Mutt was not liable for the guard that went with the Swami on tour (G.O. 857 of 19 Dec 1923: one Biradari of Silledars and an infantry guard) and set the Rs 756-6-0 due to the Mutt against its dues.

notes: The Parakala Mutt has a Palace Barr Pahare of 6 sepoys and 2 officers, not a military guard. A later letter says the enhanced contribution was ordered from January 1929.

The Executive Engineer needed Rs 15,000 for initial special repairs and Rs 2,450 a year for road repairs, while the Board's total income from the Jahagir area would be about Rs 3,067.

The Agent (3 May 1930) asked that paddy fields of about 55 acres, assessed at Rs 190, be excluded from the municipal area as Mutt land not handed over to the Municipality.

what_is_said: Bulletins (c. Nov 1930) on the health of the Swami (Chandrasekhara Bharati), who had a mental illness. He improved, had lucid intervals, read the Vivekachudamani, moved his lodging to Satchidananda Vilas across the river, and by late November was reported fully restored to normal health (Senior Surgeon to Chief Secretary).

what_is_said: In a srimukha of 22 Apr 1931 to the Maharaja, Chandrasekhara Bharati Swami nominated the brahmachari Srinivasa Sastry, son of Vedamurti (Bangalore) Rama Sastry, who had studied in the Mutt for a year, for sanyasa and eventual succession. G.O. No. 2505-17-Muz. 299-30-4 of 18 May 1931 approved the nomination on behalf of the Maharaja; no proclamation was issued because the peetha was not vacant. The Muzrai Commissioner and the DC, Kadur, attended the induction on 22 May 1931 and the boy was given the name Sri Abhinava Vidyatirtha, with a procession of both Swamis round the town.

what_is_said: Agent N.S. Nanjundaiah asked (Aug 1931) that the Agent and the Deputy Amildar continue as President and Vice-President of the new Sringeri Municipal Council. Asked whether he would give up his Deputy Commissioner-like powers of control over the Council if made President, the Agent replied (Oct 1931) that the Jagadguru, as Jahgirdar, did not wish him to resign those powers. He would serve as President only while keeping them.

notes: See next file: Government instead made the Deputy Amildar President.

Only four candidates stood and were declared elected. By notification the Deputy Amildar of the Sringeri Jahgir was made President and Honnavalli Anniah Heggade nominated Vice-President (late 1931).

notes: Elected included Javagal Naga Bhatta and Baggunji Lingiah Setty.

what_is_said: The Comptroller (1934) asked that the Sringeri Municipality open an account in the Government Treasury at Koppa. It was transacting all its business in the Jahagir Treasury, so Government dues (Local Fund Dispensary contributions, pension contributions) could not be enforced, and the Jahgir paid it no interest. The audit of 9-10 Mar 1934 found careless accounts under President K. Subramanya Sastry, Deputy Amildar.

what_is_said: Senior Surgeon's reports (1933) on the health of the Senior Jagadguru: in August he was 'perturbed in mind again and subject to hallucinations' and violent. By 10 Sep 1933 he was improving with long lucid intervals but not free from hallucinations. The reports were put before the Maharaja.
quote: Assistant Surgeon, Sringeri, to say that His Holiness the Senior Swami is perturbed in nind again and subject to hel- lucinations.

what_is_said: Final Notes of 9 Nov 1933 and Sept 1934. The Senior Swami was mentally ill, the junior Swami had fever, and Agent N.S. Nanjundaiya wanted to resign. Ex-Agent Srikanta Sastri proposed that the Senior Swami go to Kaladi, that the junior Swami be kept at the Sankaralaya, Mysore, for five years of education, and that a new Agent be appointed. Government considered taking over the Jahgir under s.25 of the Muzrai Regulation but deferred to the Swami. After the Muzrai Commissioner (N. Madhava Rao) visited on 17-18 Aug 1934, Government Order of 17 Sep 1934 appointed C. Rama Rao, Amildar of Kadur, as 'Agent' for two years ('Administrator' rejected). He had Deputy Commissioner powers under s.99 of the LR Code and pensionary contribution was to be recovered. Government stated that 'the responsibility for the management vests with the Swamigalu and not with Government'.
quote: would like to make it clear that the responsibility for the management vests with the Swamigalu end not with Government
notes: Srikanta Sastri went to South India in 1934 to manage the Mutt properties there. K. Gundu Rao was also proposed in 1933. This is the precursor of the 1935 takeover.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner forwards (Mar 1936) the Officer-in-Charge's note on the maṭh's properties outside Mysore, "the bulk" in Madras Presidency, earlier managed by N. Srikantha Sastry under a special power of attorney of 5-4-1934: Tavatherandal inam (719 acres, kist Rs 164) for Candramaulīśvara; five Ramnad villages gifted by Bhaskara Sethupathi (1864/1894) for Śāradā-Candramaulīśvara; Sendanadi and two Tirupattur houses taken by mortgage (22-6-1934) from the defaulting local agent Subramanya Iyer for ~Rs 14,000; 11½/28 shares of Pudurvalasai bought from Maddur Chandramouliswara Sastri for a Rs 27,000 loan from the Kaladi Veda Pathasala fund; a maṭh and three houses at Rameswaram (one bought for Rs 4,000); a maṭh at Madura; Travancore cash grant Rs 494 a year plus 26 acres at Kaladi; Coimbatore lands at Avanasi (179 acres, leased 99 years for Rs 1,400), Pudukarai/Savandapur (bought for a Rs 20,000 loan), Perumughai (mortgaged for Rs 15,000+1,200), Kadathur/Karatholam (for a Rs 45,000 loan to K. Narayana Sastry), Kangayam; Chinnamapet inam village (Tiruttani); and in Bombay/States Gangapur (Gadag, gift of Saka 1652), Paravi Basapur (gift of 1785-86), Pimpalgaon (Rahuri, gift of Madaji Sindia 1793-94, income made over to the Nasik maṭh), Gajendragad/Hebballi and Konanur (Ramdurg). Srikanta Sastry's letter of 17-3-1936 lists his six acts (Gobichettipalayam purchase for Rs 20,000; Rs 19,250 hypothecation from Akhilandammal; Benares/Rameswaram compromise; Rs 29,160 purchase from Laxmiammal; Sendanadi mortgage; Coimbatore suit O.S. 218/1935). Officer-in-Charge Y. Srikantaiya toured Madura/Ramnad (1936) and again 1938-39: income from Ramnad villages fell from >Rs 10,000 to negligible, agent irregular, accounts proposed to be controlled from Sringeri; Government obtained a general power of attorney from the Swami (7 May 1936).
quote: The Mutt owns extensive properties in the Madras and Bombay Presidencies and in some Native States. The bulk of the properties are in the Nadras Presidency.
notes: Long file 1936-39 (catalogue year 1935). Includes full text of the Swami's Special Power of Attorney to N. Srikantha Sastry (5-4-1934), revoking pro tanto N. S. Nanjundiah's general PoA of 5-7-1931. Branch maṭhs "managed by the local people by means of subscription" — list referred to but not legible. Figures for some acreages garbled (e.g. Pudurvalasai loan given as Rs 27,000 in one note and Rs 29,900 in another). Honorary Agent suggested entrusting the Pannandai division villages to the Raja of Ramnad (1939). Links: n=29, 43, 45, 48, 51, 52.

what_is_said: Final Note of the First Member of Council: the Swami (Candraśekhara Bhāratī) again ill and "mentally affected"; lending a Government officer to work under the maṭh (orders of 9-11-1933 and 30-8-1934) is unsatisfactory. With the Dewan's concurrence and the Maharaja's sanction, Government order (30 Jan 1936) takes the Sringeri Mutt with all its endowments and properties under Government management under Sec. 25(3) of the Mysore Religious and Charitable Institutions Regulation VII of 1927 for two years in the first instance; Agent C. Rama Rao reverted, Y. Srikantaiya appointed Officer-in-Charge under the Deputy Commissioner, Kadur. The Junior Swami to be moved to Bangalore/Mysore for study; the Muzrai Commissioner advised waiting (Feb 1936) as the Senior Swami asks for him in lucid intervals.

what_is_said: After the takeover the Muzrai Commissioner asks (Feb-Mar 1936) that Madras, Travancore, Bombay and the States (Ramdurg, Gajendragad) be notified through the Resident to give facilities to the Officer-in-Charge. A village-by-village list of Madras/Travancore properties with local managers is sent (May 1936). Bombay Government (7 May 1936) instructs the Commissioners of Central and Southern Divisions; Madras G.O. Ms. 1216 (4 Jun 1936) directs Collectors to help the local managers collect revenue. Travancore's annual varshasanam of Rs 495-1-5 (1936-37) is paid via K. Sambasiva Sastri, Curator, Oriental Manuscripts Library, Trivandrum (1937).

what_is_said: Chief Secretary's note (Jan 1936): Agent C. Government (G.O. 25-2-1936) sanction Rs 100 p.m. local allowance to Y. Srikantaiya, Officer-in-Charge, from maṭh funds.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner approves (Mar 1936), and Government confirm, the Deputy Commissioner's advice that tenants of the Sringeri Jahgir may continue to pay kandayam in kind (paddy and areca) until things settle down; the Officer-in-Charge had sold about 600 maunds of areca at Rs 5-1-0 a maund.

The Comptroller cites a 1910 precedent waiving contributions for Barr sepoys lent to the Sringeri and Raghavendraswami maṭhs.

what_is_said: Muzrai Commissioner visited Sringeri (6-8 Apr 1936): the recovered Senior Swami was satisfied with Government management, had himself been thinking of asking for it, was dissatisfied with C. Rama Rao, and said money had to be borrowed even for normal services; he asked only that internal arrangements and services not be disturbed. The Junior Swami had been drawn into an agitation against the takeover by local people including Rama Rao; both Swamis agreed he should complete his studies away from Sringeri. He left Sringeri on 21 Jun 1936 for the Shankara Mutt, Bangalore; Government sanction an establishment (teacher, manager, attendants, two student stipends) costing Rs 189 p.m. from the maṭh's closing balance (1936-37 budget surplus est. Rs 10,292).
quote: The Junior Swamigalu was drawn into this agitation by certain local people including Mr. C. Rama Rao, the Agent of the Mutt.
notes: Deputy Commissioner noted the takeover was legal only during the Swami's disability (Sec. 25 proviso) so his consent was needed after recovery. Plan first for Mysore Abhinava Shankaralaya, finally Bangalore. Link n=57 (return 1937).

Puttanna) found him raving, shouting and beating himself in Narasimhavana; DMO judged him "mentally unsound" and asked for the Superintendent of the Mental Hospital; Deputy Commissioner held the Jahgir could not be left to the Swami or to the Agent, "a local man with a lot of local prejudices". Leads directly to the takeover (n=28).

what_is_said: The maṭh owed Rs 75,000 and odd to the Bank of Mysore, the Sringeri Municipality (municipal funds in the Jahgir treasury), Government (arrears of education and local cesses ~Rs 3,300) and private individuals, while about two lakhs it had lent out could not be recovered in the depression; temple buildings needed urgent repair. The Officer-in-Charge and Deputy Commissioner asked for Rs 60,000 over 15 years; the Muzrai Commissioner recommended Rs 75,000 at 5% repayable in ten annual instalments adjusted from the annual sayer compensation of Rs 15,000, financed by selling 5% Mysore Loan Bonds of the General Muzrai Fund or Chattram Savings Fund; the Swami agreed; Financial Secretary, Second Member and the Maharaja sanctioned (Aug 1936).

what_is_said: C. Rama Rao, Amildar, Agent of the maṭh from Sep 1934 (two years, rank of Assistant Commissioner), retired 8 Apr 1936 amid complaints. Charges proved: drew an unauthorised advance of Rs 1,025 (Nov 1935) when maṭh servants were unpaid and manipulated accounts via the Nanjangud Pathasala fund and Sharada Bank shares (Rs 18,000); tried to exchange his old house for two maṭh houses; encouraged the Junior Swami to protest against the takeover; called a Shimoga lawyer against Government in Feb 1936. Muzrai Commissioner proposed a 10% pension cut for life; First Member, Dewan and Second Member reduced it to six months (Sep 1936).

what_is_said: Final Note of the First Member of Council (agreed by the Dewan, submitted to the Maharaja): the Matt with all its endowments and properties, taken under Government management by G.O. 1028-30/Muz.174-35-2 of 30 Jan 1936 for two years with Asst Commissioner Y. Srikantiah as Officer-in-charge under the Deputy Commissioner, Kadur, is to remain under Government management until further orders, with Srikantiah continuing. The Muzrai Commissioner, after interviewing the Swami at Sringeri on 19-21 Nov 1937, reported that the Swami appreciated the 'quiet and efficient' management and himself asked for its continuance; the D.C. Kadur had noted the two-year period expired on 30 Jan 1938. The file also carries the 1959 order restoring the Matt's properties in and outside the State to the Matt's own management after the abolition of the Sringeri Jahgir.

what_is_said: Progress reports (Sept 1939-Oct 1940) from the Officer-in-charge through the D.C. Subramanya Iyer. Government, finding collections unsatisfactory, ordered (March 1940) the Officer-in-charge's allowance stopped pending explanation; land-revenue collection in the Jahagir proper was only 75% of current demand, and the sale of Pudur Valasai and Sendanadi was dropped for the present (Oct 1940).

Satyanarayana Rao, vakil of Anantapur. As the Matt had had no income since 1926-27, Government (G.O. 20-8-1940) sanctioned, on the Muzrai Commissioner's and D.C.'s recommendation and the Swami's wish, purchase of the other half for Rs 1,000 from Matt funds (credited with Sri Lakshamma's Rs 495 endowment and a Rs 500 loan of the Bangalore Pathasala fund). The whole village is 236 a 2 g (86 a 19 g uncultivable), assessed Rs 242-2-0, income about Rs 220 of which Rs 178-14-0 is paid to Government; the sale deed was postponed to summer 1941.

Kadur held this contrary to the Account Rules but confirmed that under G.O.s of Jan 1937 and Nov 1938 the Swami could reappropriate within the heads Matha, Temples in Sringeri and Annachatra; Government agreed that the budget provision could be increased if needed and amounts reappropriated from savings under other heads.

The Muzrai Commissioner noted this permanent alienation conflicted with Sec. 30 of the Religious and Charitable Institutions Act; Government asked for the Swami's wishes, and the Swami agreed only to the darkhast disposal of banjar lands of the Matt's villages in the State; sanction sought accordingly.

It had had no patel for two years, raiyats owed the Matt Rs 356 odd, Rs 113-12-5 jodi arrears and Rs 110 survey dues were owed to Government, and the village was 'mismanaged'. Under Revenue Secretary's instructions (12 Mar 1925) the DC took the village under Government management, approved as a temporary measure pending recognition of Subrahmanya Sastry of Udayagiri.

places: Avani (Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar District); Kolar; Bowringpet; Mahabubabad (Hyderabad State); Rajakal (Gudiyatham Taluk, North Arcot); Vaniyambadi; Devarayasamudra; Bangalore
what_is_said: Succession to the Avani Matt after Sri Vidyasankara Bharathi Swamigalu died at Mahabubabad, Hyderabad State, on 11 Apr 1925. Petitions and printed memorials argue whether a householder or a brahmachari should succeed, and whether the Sringeri Mutt should choose. Government notified a meeting of disciples at King Edward Hall, Bowringpet, for 3 Apr 1926 (Notification 22 Feb 1926). The Kolar DC reported that a Velanadu brahmachari was wanted and that Sringeri be asked to select.
quote: at no time in the history of the Avani Mutt has the choice of a successor been allowed to be determined by any other Mutt, as the Avani Mutt has ever claimed absolute independence
notes: ORIGIN claim: 'Avani Mutt itself was founded by Sri Vidyaranya who had been a householder' (one petitioner, OCR 'Vidyrsenya'). Memorialists propose Y. Subba Rau, Sanskrit teacher at Chamarajendra Sanskrit College. Catalogue title 'affairs reorganized' is not matched in the legible text; the outcome is not in the file.

places: Kudli (Shimoga Taluk); Shimoga District; Bombay Presidency
what_is_said: First Member of Council proposes exempting Sri Valukeswara Bharathi Swamigalu from personal appearance in civil courts as his predecessors were. He describes the Kudli Sringeri Matt as one of the most important Smartha Matts, entitled to all Sringeri honours except adda palakki, with extensive lands in Shimoga District and the Bombay Presidency.
quote: the Swamigalu of the Natt is en- titled to all the honours granted to the Swamigalu of the Sringeri att except the Adda Palakki.
notes: Confirms the outcome of the adda-palakki dispute (K02-K06).

what_is_said: The Matt asked for 2 years' arrears of its annual sandalwood grant (years Rudhirodgari and Raktakshi). The Conservator of Forests (9 Jan 1926) says the supply lapsed under G.O. 454-65 of 28 July 1922 because it was not drawn by the end of February. The Muzrai Commissioner recommends supply, as the Swami could not press the claim while his succession was unrecognised.

notes: Revenue in kind from the State (sandalwood); see K10.

what_is_said: The Matt had contributed Rs 840 a year out of its tasdik grant for Sanskrit scholarships (Advaita Vedanta at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore; Sahitya and Krishna Yajurveda in Bangalore / Chamarajendra Veda Maha Patasala) under G.O. 27 Aug 1919, which pooled Rs 1,065 from the Kudli, Ahobila, Sripadaraya and Krishnananda Matts. The new Swami asked to withdraw it for a Veda Patasala in the Matt. G.O. 1080-83 Muz. 277-25-11 of 10 Dec 1926 approved discontinuing it from 1925-26.

what_is_said: On the Swami's application for a rahadari to tour the State, officials found no grant authority for 'ambari on elephant', which the 1908 list of honours had accepted on precedent; the Uttaradi Mutt also has it. The Dewan opposed it as exceptional. His Highness ordered (Dec 1927) that, given precedent, the ambari on an elephant be included.
quote: His Highness the Mahareje considers that in view of the precedent the ambari with en elephant should be included among the honovrs to be allowed.
notes: Nirup R.Dis. 87/1927-28 dated 23 Dec 1927 (cited in K30).

what_is_said: The Sarvadhikari of the Matt (letter 15 May 1929) reports that Siva Bhatta alias Narasimha Bharati Swami has published notices appointing one Mallari Dikshit (Sureswara Sankara Bharati) as his successor to the Kudli Sringeri peetha. The Muzrai Commissioner advises no notice be taken, as that claim and his predecessors' were rejected by G.O. 1554/M.F.172-22-3 of 14 Oct 1922; the recognised Swami's succession stands under G.O. 1843-5 of 22 June 1925.

places: Chitradurga; Davangere; Jagalur; Harihar; Shimoga; Tarikere; Kadur District
what_is_said: During the Swami's 1931 tour, the DC Chitradurga asked whether 'Ane mele ambari' in the 1927 rahadari meant riding in the howdah or only leading an elephant with an empty one, fearing Lingayat objections (the Swami was held up at Davangere for nearly a fortnight in 1904/05). The Agent protested; the Muzrai Commissioner cited the Uttaradi Mutt. G.O. 729 Muz. 116-31-3 of 20 Nov 1931 held that the insignia authorises the Swami to sit in the ambari and go in procession, and the procession then went off well.
quote: The object of giving this insignia to the Swami is to sit in the Ambari on an elephant's back and go in procession if
notes: He rode in the ambari at Shimoga, Tarikere, Jagalur and Harihar without trouble. The DC notes the previous visit to Chitradurga was in 1904.

places: Kudli (Shimoga Taluk); properties inside and outside Mysore State; Gudibanda
what_is_said: At the Swami's request (Srimukha 1933), Government (G.O. 641-2 Muz. 65-33-4, 10/11 Nov 1933) took over management of the Matt's lands in and outside the State for one year, at Rs 4,077 a year in costs, with a Deputy Amildar as Agent. The Muzrai Commissioner put income at Rs 35,046-13-6: villages in the State Rs 4,499, outside Rs 10,504; sircar lands in the State Rs 1,095, outside Rs 6,294; varshasana from disciples Rs 1,024; other items about Rs 11,630. The Matt estimated land income at Rs 22,000. The internal management of the Matt and its branches stays with the Matt.

what_is_said: Tour of Sri Abhinavoddanda Vidyaranya Bharathi Swamigalu of the Avani Sringeri Mutt: a three-day stay and procession in the Bangalore Civil and Military Station from 5 July 1934. Mysore asked the Resident for police arrangements; the Resident ordered that the procession avoid streets with Muhammadan places of worship. His birudus are those in a rahadari of 8 Dec 1894 (Honours Manual). A loan of Rs 600 was recommended in connection with the tour.

what_is_said: Sri Vidyabhinava Valukeswara Bharathi Swamigalu died at Mysore on 10 Apr 1936 without a successor. His predecessor Valukeswara Bharati, still alive, had handed over the peetha by a registered Adhikara Patra (G.O. 1069-72 of 19 Jan 1933) while keeping some properties, so the Law Department was asked whether he could nominate. On a petition of disciples at Mysore, Government (G.O. 1481-83 of 23 Apr 1936) sanctioned the installation of Vedamurthi Mahadeva Sastry, the late Swami's nephew, done on 24 Apr 1936.
quote: Mysore, wherein they requested that Vedamurthi Mahadeva Sastry, nephew of the deceased Swamigalu in his purvasrama, may be instélked
notes: Catalogue year 1935; events April 1936. The 1932 succession (Nov 1932) was by relinquishment, not death. The new Swami took the title Sachidananda Sankara Bharati (K40).

what_is_said: Telephone message from the Palace: the dying Kudli Swami at Mysore wanted a Dharwar pandit as successor (first choices declined), then his son-in-law Subba Sastry. Without one there would be litigation, 'as there are two previous Swamies alive, and one of them had carried litigation to the Privy Council'. On his death (10 Apr 1936) the DC Mysore took temporary management of the Matt and inventoried its belongings; the Shimoga Amildar sealed five almirahs of documents at Kudli, and other taluks' Amildars were told to secure the immovable properties.
quote: If the present Swami dies with- out initiating his successor, there is Likelihood of litigation as there are two previous Swamies alive,
notes: Nagesa Sastry of Dharwar was the Matt's Agent. 'No Pandit of Mysore is considered to be desirable for this place, and it is only a Pandit of Dharwar that should be selected': the Matt's following was centred in Dharwar.

what_is_said: Government management (continued to the end of Jan 1936 by Pro. 914-17 of 26/29 Dec 1934) is extended a further three years, to the end of January 1939, at the Swami's request, keeping the Agency office at Bangalore with the same pay, contingencies and travelling allowance (G.O. 946-49 of 10 Jan 1936).

places: Kudli (Shimoga Taluk); Bellary District; Anantapur District; Donur; Bangalore
what_is_said: After the Swami's death (10 Apr 1936) management continued under Section 25(2) of the Mysore Religious and Charitable Institutions Regulation, and the Government Agent kept looking after properties outside Mysore. Mahadeva Sastri was installed on 24 Apr 1936 as Sri Sachidananda Sankara Bharati Swamigalu and asked that management stay with Government to the end of Jan 1939 under Section 25(1); Madras (G.O. Ms. 1089, 15 May 1936) renewed its instructions to the Bellary and Anantapur Collectors. A Matt suit against Vettal Krishna Kulkarni of Donur needed the new Swami substituted as plaintiff.
quote: he was inducted into Sanyas- rama and installed on the Peeta under the titular name of Sri Sachidanan- da Sankara Bharati Swamigalu on Friday the 24th instant.
notes: Catalogue year 1935; content Apr-May 1936. Legal basis of State management: Mysore Religious and Charitable Institutions Regulation s.25(1)/(2).

what_is_said: Recovery of amounts due from one Hutchu Rao for the Matt's properties in Sangli State and Venkatapura village: private settlement failed, the Government Agent filed four suits, and the Muzrai Commissioner sanctioned Rs 300 from Matt funds for costs (order C.349/35-36, 14 Oct 1935). The Comptroller agreed that Government sanction for such advances is unnecessary when Mutts are under temporary Government management via powers of attorney.
quote: it is reported by the Government agent that as negotiations for a private settlement failed, four suits were filed within the period for limitation.
notes: Venkatapura's taluk/district is not given (probably Bombay side). Hutchu Rao was presumably a former lessee or agent.

places: Dharwar District; Bijapur District; Udagatti (Ranibennur Taluk, Dharwar District)
what_is_said: Succession nazarana on the Matt's inams in Bombay: after the Nov 1932 succession the Collector of Dharwar levied Rs 2,745-15-0 and the Collector of Bijapur Rs 1,166-14-6, each in four instalments. After the April 1936 succession Dharwar again demanded Rs 2,745-15-0 from 1936-37. Mysore, through the Resident (19 Oct 1936), asked exemption under Bombay Act II of 1863 s.8(3). Bombay refused: the inams were granted 'to Shankarbha(rati) and his successors' on condition of nazarana and so carry a personal element (as decided in 1874), and arrears must be paid. The Mamlatdar of Ranibennur pressed collection in 1937.

notes: Shows the Bombay inams were personal grants to the guru line, not temple holdings. The Matt is known locally as 'Uddughatti Mutt' after Udagatti, Ranibennur Taluk. Also cites Bombay G.R. 28 Aug 1874 and Act XI of 1852.

what_is_said: Restoration: Government management (since Nov 1933, last extended by G.O. 831-3 of 25 Nov 1938 to Jan 1942) is handed back to the Swami from 1 Mar 1941 (he asked for 1 Feb 1941), on his signing the usual indemnity bond for officials. The Swami had ordered reforms in external and internal management on taking back the properties.
